newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's children paying price for reforms.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's children paying price for reforms.

text.p: Vietnam's 10-year-old economic reform process is being accompanied by growing problems of child abuse and destitution, a government childcare official said on Thursday.

Tran Thi Thanh-Thanh of the Vietnam Committee for the Protection and Care of Children told a meeting in Hanoi that despite improvements in child healthcare and education, Vietnam's economic boom was creating new problems.

"In parallel with economic successes, we are now confronting new challenges," she said. "...those are street children earning their bread in cities coming from the countryside, the child victims of sexual and drug abuse."
Thanh said there were currently tens of thousands of child victims of such evils in Vietnam.
She called for strict punishment of offenders and community education programmes to tackle the problem.
Vietnam introduced capitalist-style reforms to its Soviet-style economy in the late 1980s, resulting in marked improvements in the standard of living, especially in the cities.
But growing affluence and a yawning rural-urban wealth gap have created new problems.

Social workers say between 22,000 and 50,000 children, most from poor country areas, are earning a living for themselves and their families by begging, or worse, on the streets of Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi.
The number is small compared to some other countries in the region, but concerned groups say it is on the rise.
